comments: For several 'resources spared' judgments (e.g., Scenario 1 C, Scenario 4 E), an option that helps others directly (using a shared vehicle, shifting burden to family) is hard to separate from one that simply avoids using resources at all; I treated heavier use of a shared/communal resource as lower-scoring even when it benefited others, per the instruction to rate only what is used, not kindness.

Scenario 3's reversibility measure had little textual basis for most options besides B (explicit hold-back) and C ('a sealed draw'); rankings among A/D/E/F rely on secondary inference about how easily each allocation method could be revised before doses are given.
